key_insight: SPARC uses longitudinal health measurements to predict cancer-related adverse events, focusing on toxicity risk rather than drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The model could support toxicity-prevention research by identifying high-risk patients, including those potentially most likely to benefit from G-CSF.
method: Transformer-based foundation model using routinely collected longitudinal health measurements.
Pre-trained and fine-tuned to predict cancer-related adverse events.
Compared pooled multi-institution with single-institution fine-tuning for generalizability.
evidence_signal: Development used 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients; evaluation included held-out data, a prospective same-center cohort of 23,126 patients, public external datasets totaling 26,012 patients, and external multi-hospital cohorts of 562,620 and 206,840 patients.
watch_item: The abstract reports predictive performance but does not establish that model-guided care improves patient outcomes.
paper_title: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
